TORONTO, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Barrick Mining Corporation (NYSE:B)(TSX:ABX) has received notice of an unsolicited mini-tender offer made by New York Stock and Bond LLC (“NYSB”) to purchase up to 50,000 of Barrick’s common shares at a below-market price of US$26.40 per share. NYSB’s below-market offer price of US$26.40 per share represents a discount of approximately 34.91% to the closing price of Barrick common shares on the New York Stock Exchange on November 6, 2026, the last trading day before the mini-tender offer was commenced. Barrick shareholders who tender their shares in this offer will receive a below-market price.

Barrick recommends shareholders do not tender their shares in response to this unsolicited mini-tender offer because the offer is at a price below the current market price of Barrick’s shares and is subject to numerous conditions. Barrick shareholders who have already tendered their shares may withdraw their shares no more than 14 days after the date of delivery of the shareholder’s acceptance form to the depositary for this offer, in accordance with NYSB’s offer documentation. The offer is currently scheduled to expire at 5:00 p.m., Eastern time, on November 8, 2027, unless it is extended or earlier revoked by NYSB.

Barrick does not endorse NYSB’s unsolicited offer and is not in any way affiliated or associated with NYSB, its offer, or the offer documentation.

Mini-tender offers are designed to avoid investor protections such as disclosure and procedural requirements applicable to most take-over bids and tender offers under Canadian and U.S. securities laws. Both Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) recommend that investors exercise caution with mini-tender offers and have expressed serious concerns about mini-tender offers, including the possibility that investors might tender to such offers without understanding the offer price relative to the actual market price of their securities.

The SEC has issued “Tips for Investors” regarding mini-tender offers, noting that some bidders, in making the offers at below-market prices, are “hoping that they will catch investors off guard if the investors do not compare the offer price to the current market price.” The SEC’s advisory may be found on the SEC website at http://www.sec.gov/investor/pubs/minitend.htm.

The CSA's long-standing guidance on mini-tenders can be found on the Ontario Securities Commission website at www.osc.gov.on.ca/en/SecuritiesLaw_csa_19991210_61-301.jsp.

Brokers, dealers, and other market participants are encouraged to exercise caution and review the letter regarding broker-dealer mini-tender offer dissemination and disclosures on the SEC website at www.sec.gov/divisions/marketreg/minitenders/sia072401.htm.

Barrick shareholders are urged to obtain current market quotations for their shares, consult with their broker or financial advisor, and exercise caution with respect to NYSB’s unsolicited offer.

Barrick requests that a copy of this news release be included in any distribution to Barrick shareholders of materials relating to NYSB’s mini-tender offer for Barrick common shares.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - Noble Plains Uranium Corp. (TSXV: NOBL) (OTCQB: NBLXF) (FSE: INE0) ("Noble Plains" or the "Company"), a U.S.-focused uranium exploration and development company, is pleased to announce that it has entered into a loan agreement (the "Loan Agreement") with Eagle Nuclear Energy Corp. (NASDAQ: NUCL) ("Eagle"), pursuant to which Eagle has agreed to make available to the Company a secured loan in the maximum principal amount of $500,000 (the "Bridge Loan"). The Loan Agreement has been entered into as part of the proposed transaction (the "Proposed Transaction") detailed in the binding letter of intent (the "LOI") announced by the Company in its news release dated November 4, 2026, and providing for the acquisition, by Eagle, of all of the issued and outstanding common shares of the Company by way of a court-approved plan of arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia).

The Bridge Loan will be secured by a guarantee from the Company's Arizona subsidiary and security interests granted by the Company and certain of its subsidiaries over their respective present and after-acquired personal property, subject to the terms of the Loan Agreement and related security documents. The Bridge Loan is intended to provide the Company with funding for general working capital and corporate purposes and transaction costs relating to the Proposed Transaction.

The Bridge Loan will be made available to the Company in two tranches. An initial advance of CAD $150,000 (the "First Tranche") will be disbursed to the Company upon the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions precedent set out in the Loan Agreement and the other applicable security documents, including receipt of all necessary approvals from the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV") in connection with the Bridge Loan.

Following the disbursement of the First Tranche, an additional advance of CAD $350,000 will be disbursed to the Company after the execution and delivery of the arrangement agreement (the "Arrangement Agreement") by the Company and Eagle, subject to the terms and conditions of the Loan Agreement. The Arrangement Agreement, under which the Proposed Transaction would be completed, remains subject to negotiation between the parties.

The outstanding principal amount of the Bridge Loan will bear interest at a fixed interest rate of 10% per annum, calculated daily on the basis of a 365-day year.

The Bridge Loan, together with all accrued and unpaid interest and other amounts owing under the Loan Agreement, will mature on the earliest of: (i) the date that is 180 days following the date the LOI is terminated for any reason (except if as a result of the Arrangement Agreement being entered into) or the Arrangement Agreement is terminated for any reason, other than with respect to a superior proposal; (ii) the date of completion of the Proposed Transaction; and (iii) the date that is five business days following the date of termination in the event the LOI or the Arrangement Agreement is terminated pursuant to a superior proposal.

The Bridge Loan and the advance of funds thereunder remain subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the applicable conditions precedent in the Loan Agreement, including the completion and delivery of the applicable security documents and receipt of all necessary approvals from the TSXV.

Noble Plains Uranium Corp. is a U.S.-focused uranium exploration and development company advancing a portfolio of high-potential projects amenable to In Situ Recovery (ISR), the most capital-efficient and environmentally responsible method of uranium extraction. Our strategy targets historically drilled and underexplored assets in proven jurisdictions, with the objective of rapidly delineating NI 43-101-compliant resources and building a scalable inventory of domestic uranium.

Vancouver, BC – November 20, 2026 – TheNewswire - Copper One Resources Corp. (“Copper One”) (CSE: CEXY | OTCID: CEXYF | FSE: IW8 | WKN: A42AGR) (the “Company”) announces that it has entered into an option agreement dated November XX, 2026 with an arm’s-length vendor to acquire an undivided 100% interest in the Quatum Copper Project (“Quatum” or the “Project”), northeast of Campbell River, British Columbia. The Project comprises 12 mineral claims covering 3,646.90 hectares (approximately 9,011.7 acres) and two pending mineral claim applications covering an additional 746.86 hectares (approximately 1,845.5 acres). Together, the claims and applications cover 4,393.76 hectares (approximately 10,857.2 acres).

Quatum is located near the Company’s 100%-owned Redonda Copper-Molybdenum Project on West Redonda Island. The historical CAP showing in the Quatum area lies approximately 13 kilometres (8 miles) north-northeast of the RED occurrence at Redonda. This proximity provides an opportunity to evaluate coordinated exploration planning and regional logistics, while building on Copper One’s experience at Redonda.1

David Greenway, President and Chief Executive Officer of Copper One, commented: “Quatum represents an exciting opportunity for Copper One to advance a copper-bearing breccia system previously explored by Newmont. Its historical drilling and surface mineralization provide a compelling foundation for renewed exploration using modern techniques. Its proximity to our ongoing drilling at the 100%-owned Redonda Project, previously explored by Teck, strengthens the strategic fit and creates opportunities to apply our regional geological knowledge and coordinate exploration activities. Together, these projects expand our presence in British Columbia and reinforce our strategy of building a substantial North American copper portfolio. With projects across Nevada, Utah and British Columbia, Copper One is assembling multiple opportunities for discovery and growth as the world’s need for copper continues to expand.”

Quatum Project highlights

  • Government records document three diamond drill holes completed by Newmont in 1970, totaling 2,410 feet (approximately 735 metres). 

  • Historical copper mineralization associated with an intrusive breccia system near the CAP showing, with chalcopyrite and locally observed bornite. 

  • Historical Hole 1 results include 0.17% copper over 100 feet (30.48 metres), with a higher-grade interval of 0.38% copper over 10 feet (3.05 metres). These are historical reported results requiring verification. 

  • Historical surface chip sampling at location J returned a reported weighted average of 0.46% copper over 20 feet (6.10 metres). True widths are unknown. 

  • Historical mapping, soil sampling and geophysical surveys provide a basis for evaluating targets for follow-up exploration. 

Historical exploration and geological setting

The British Columbia Geological Survey identifies the CAP or QUATUM RIVER showing as a copper showing classified as a porphyry copper occurrence hosted by intrusive rocks of the Coast Plutonic Complex. Its description records chalcopyrite, pyrite and pyrrhotite mainly within a breccia pipe hosted by quartz monzonite and quartz diorite.2

British Columbia’s Geology, Exploration and Mining 1970 (p. 229) records three surface diamond drill holes totalling 2,410 feet (approximately 735 metres) on the Cap 2 claim, together with geological mapping, 6.6 line-miles (approximately 10.6 line-kilometres) of magnetometer and induced polarization surveys, and 296 soil samples.3

Historical information and data verification

The historical exploration information is drawn from government publications and archived reports and memoranda prepared in 1970 and 1971. It is presented to explain the basis for further investigation and is not current verified exploration data. Drill lengths are downhole lengths, surface results are sample lengths, and true widths are unknown. Visual sulphide observations, including bornite and chalcopyrite, do not establish copper grade or economic significance. Float is transported material and may not represent the underlying bedrock.

The records reviewed do not provide a complete set of drill assay certificates, collar coordinates, sampling and recovery records, analytical procedures or quality assurance and quality control documentation. About Copper One Resources Corp.

Copper One Resources Corp. is focused on identifying, acquiring and advancing high-potential copper, copper-silver-gold and copper-molybdenum projects to help meet global demand for critical metals used in electrification, AI infrastructure and data centres, renewable energy, defence and power system modernization.

The Company's flagship asset is the Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold District, located approximately 156 miles (251 kilometres) from Reno, Nevada. Majuba Hill is an exploration-stage porphyry copper project situated in an established mining jurisdiction with existing infrastructure, where ongoing exploration is focused on evaluating the scale and continuity of a copper-silver-gold mineralized system.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Redonda Copper-Molybdenum Project, located northeast of Campbell River in British Columbia's Vancouver Mining Division. The district-scale project comprises approximately 2,746.46 hectares (6,787 acres) across nine mineral claims and hosts a porphyry-style copper-molybdenum system within the Coast Suture Zone, a geological belt known for porphyry copper and skarn mineralization. In addition, Copper One holds an option to earn up to a 100% interest in the Redhill Property, located south of Ashcroft, British Columbia, adjacent to the Trans-Canada Highway. The 4,736-hectare (11,703-acre) property hosts volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) mineralization prospective for copper, zinc, silver and gold, while also demonstrating potential for epithermal gold mineralization.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Sport Project in Utah through its wholly owned subsidiary, Rooinek Mining Corp., expanding the Company’s portfolio of North American copper exploration assets.

SINGAPORE--(BUSINESS WIRE)--TechCreate Group Ltd. (OTCMKTS: TCGLF) (“TechCreate” or the “Company”), a technology consultancy and advanced software solutions provider specializing in payment solutions, cybersecurity, and digital services, announced that the NYSE American Committee for Review (the “Committee”) has unanimously determined to affirm the decision of the NYSE American LLC (“NYSE American” or the “Exchange”) Listing Qualifications Panel (the “Panel”) with respect to the delisting of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares. Following its review, the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”) has determined not to pursue any further challenge to the Committee’s decision.

The Committee’s written decision, dated November 9, 2026, follows a hearing held on October 22, 2026 and affirms the Panel’s August 20, 2026 opinion, which upheld the NYSE American Staff (“Staff”) determination to commence delisting proceedings. The proceedings stem from the one-day trading suspension of the Company’s securities ordered by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) and effective on February 2, 2026, the stated basis for which was potential manipulation of the Company’s securities through social media recommendations made by unknown persons.

In reaching its determination, the Board reviewed the sequence of the appeal proceedings and the Committee’s written decision, and considered the following:

  • No finding of wrongdoing. The Committee’s decision states that the Staff’s investigation into the manipulative trading of the Company’s securities did not result in a finding of wrongdoing on the part of the Company or any of its officers and directors.
  • Exchange discretion. The Committee determined that the NYSE American Company Guide (the “Company Guide”) gives the Staff discretion to delist a security regardless of whether the issuer complies with applicable listing standards. The Committee acknowledged the preventive measures the Company put forward, including voluntary surveillance, reporting and escalation procedures, and enhanced Board oversight, but did not consider them sufficient to continue the listing.
  • Focus on the business. The Board believes the Company’s time and resources are better directed to operating and growing the business, and to evaluating alternatives intended to protect the interests of shareholders.

Under Section 1206 of the Company Guide, the Committee’s decision may be called for review by the Exchange’s Board of Directors at the request of one or more of its directors. If the decision is not called for review, the Company will be notified that it represents the final action of the Exchange. If the decision is not called for review and the Company receives such notice, the Exchange is expected to proceed with delisting of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares. The Company’s securities continue to be quoted in the over-the-counter market under the symbol TCGLF.

About TechCreate Group Ltd.

TechCreate Group Ltd. is a Singapore-based payment software solutions provider. Founded in 2015, the Company delivers digital payment and infrastructure solutions to financial institutions, telecommunications companies, deposit insurers and enterprises. TechCreate’s offerings include real-time payment systems, digital banking platforms, API management, cybersecurity and cloud computing. Its proprietary Artificial Intelligence Real-Time Engine (AI-RTE) is designed to enable fast, secure and efficient payment processing. For more information, visit https://www.techcreate.com.sg/.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - Allied Critical Metals Inc. (CSE: ACM) (OTCQB: ACMIF) (FSE: 0VJ0) ("Allied" or the "Company") is providing the results of its annual shareholder meeting and a general corporate update on certain of its prior disclosure.

Clarifying Technical Disclosure

As a result of a review by the British Columbia Securities Commission, the Company is clarifying certain scientific and technical disclosure regarding its Borralha Tungsten Project ("Borralha") and Vila Verde Tungsten Project ("Vila Verde") in northern Portugal.

The Company has identified restricted and potentially ambiguous disclosures in certain of its news releases, the third quarter 2026 corporate presentation (the "Presentation"), website and related investor relations materials under National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects ("NI 43-101"). The Company is retracting and clarifying the disclosure identified below, including statements concerning the preliminary economic assessment for Borralha (the "PEA"), the historical estimates at Vila Verde, production decisions and qualified person identification.

The PEA is preliminary in nature and includes Inferred Mineral Resources that are considered too speculative geologically to have the economic considerations applied to them that would enable them to be categorized as Mineral Reserves. There is no certainty that the PEA results will be realized. Mineral Resources are not Mineral Reserves and do not have demonstrated economic viability.

The following corrections relate to the Company's March 2, 2026 news release entitled "Allied Critical Metals Delivers Robust Initial PEA at the Borralha Project" (the "March Release"), the Presentation, website and related investor relations materials. Investors should not rely on the statements and presentations of information expressly retracted below. This news release presents the Borralha PEA base-case economic results alongside two lower-price and two higher-price sensitivities on a consistent basis. This news release does not restate the PEA's numerical economic results.

  • "Robust Economics". The Company retracts the characterization "Robust Initial PEA" in the March Release's headline, "Robust Economics" in its Key Highlights, and the statement in the CEO quotation that the initial PEA "confirms the Borralha Project as a high-return, capital-efficient tungsten development project", together with equivalent characterizations in subsequent news releases and related materials. These descriptions suggested a level of certainty inconsistent with the preliminary nature of a PEA and the cautionary disclosure required by sections 2.3(3)(a) and 3.4(e) of NI 43-101. Although the March Release included PEA cautionary language, these characterizations did not appropriately reflect those qualifications. The PEA assesses potential economic viability; it does not establish technical or economic viability. It includes inferred mineral resources that are too speculative geologically to have the economic considerations applied to them that would enable them to be categorized as mineral reserves, and there is no certainty that the PEA will be realized. Mineral resources that are not mineral reserves do not have demonstrated economic viability.
  • Higher-price scenarios and upside presentation. The March Release prominently presented a "Medium Case" and a "High Case", alongside an Argus long-term "Base Case". The Company acknowledges that the presentation of those scenarios should also have included corresponding downside sensitivity in order to provide a balanced assessment. Although Section 7.6 and Figure 1 of the March Release included a broader price sensitivity analysis, the prominent presentation of favourable scenarios was not balanced by equivalent downside disclosure alongside those scenarios. Accordingly, the Company retracts the prior unbalanced presentation and replaces it with the below restated sensitivity analysis for the Borralha Project, which presents investors with a balanced range of potential outcomes based on differing commodity price assumptions. Investors should consider all scenarios together, and no single scenario should be viewed in isolation.

The Borralha PEA mine plan was developed using a tungsten price assumption of approximately US$659/mtu WO₃. The economic Base Case applies Argus's year-by-year tungsten price forecast, which averages approximately US$704/mtu WO₃. The four sensitivity cases use the same mine plan, production schedule and other modelling assumptions, with each case applying its stated fixed tungsten price over the mine life.

The US$704/mtu WO₃ base case remains the principal case for the Borralha PEA. The table below presents the base case alongside two lower-price and two higher-price sensitivities. Each of the four sensitivity cases applies a constant tungsten price over the life of the mine using the Base Case mine plan, production schedule and other modelling assumptions. These are sensitivity cases and do not replace the base-case assumption or constitute forecasts of future prices.

The analysis varies the tungsten price while holding the mine plan, production schedule and other technical and economic assumptions constant. It therefore measures the effect of price changes on the existing PEA development case and does not represent a separately optimized mine plan for each price. The prices shown are benchmark prices. Realized tungsten revenue per mtu produced reflects concentrate payability and applicable commercial deductions, including treatment and refining charges. All-in sustaining cost (AISC) is expressed per mtu produced. As a result, the project can have a negative NPV even when the benchmark price exceeds the AISC per mtu produced. The after-tax NPV at an 8% discount rate also reflects the initial capital investment and the timing of project cash flows. At US$306/mtu and US$400/mtu WO₃, the modelled after-tax NPVs are negative US$234 million and negative US$134 million, respectively.

The lowest-price sensitivity is not presented as an economic break-even price. Economic outcomes are determined by the cash-flow model, including capital expenditure, operating costs, commercial deductions, royalties and taxation.

The PEA is preliminary and includes Inferred Mineral Resources. Their geological uncertainty precludes treating them as Mineral Reserves on the basis of this economic assessment. There is no certainty that the PEA will be realized. Mineral Resources that are not Mineral Reserves do not have demonstrated economic viability.

  • PEA results in the Presentation. The Company retracts that presentation of the PEA results in the Presentation, as the disclosure did not fully satisfy the conditions in section 2.3(3) of NI 43-101. Investors should not rely on the PEA results as presented in the Presentation. The economic results in Table 1 of this news release should be read together with the accompanying assumptions, qualifications and cautionary disclosure, including the preliminary nature of the PEA and its inclusion of Inferred Mineral Resources. The Company will ensure that future disclosure of a PEA that includes inferred mineral resources includes an explanation of the basis of the assessment and its qualifications and, with equal prominence, the caution that the assessment is preliminary in nature, includes inferred mineral resources that are too speculative geologically to have the economic considerations applied to them that would enable them to be categorized as mineral reserves, and that there is no certainty the assessment will be realized.
  • Vila Verde historical estimates. The Presentation presented historical estimate information for Vila Verde in a manner that could be interpreted as treating those estimates as current mineral resources. The Company retracts that characterization and any related disclosure in its website and investor relations materials that conveyed the same impression. A qualified person has not done sufficient work to classify the historical estimates as current mineral resources or mineral reserves, and the Company is not treating them as current mineral resources or mineral reserves. Investors should not rely on those historical estimates as current estimates. The Company will remove any presentation suggesting otherwise.
  • Production decision. The Presentation contained disclosure that could be interpreted as indicating that the Company had made a production decision. The Company retracts any implication in the Presentation that it has made a commercial production decision in respect of either Borralha or Vila Verde, including in respect of any pilot plant. The Company confirms that it has made no such decision for either project. The pilot plant testwork contemplated at Vila Verde is intended to inform further technical evaluation of that project. The Company has not completed a feasibility study supporting mineral reserves for either project, and the PEA does not establish the technical or economic viability of production or provide the same level of confidence as a feasibility study. The production schedules, mine-life estimates and processing assumptions disclosed in the March Release describe a conceptual PEA scenario, not a commitment to construct or achieve production on those schedules. The March Release identified further drilling, metallurgical testing, geotechnical and hydrogeological investigations, engineering toward a pre-feasibility study and further permitting as recommended work.
  • Qualified person identification. The Presentation did not identify the qualified person who prepared, supervised the preparation of, or approved its scientific and technical information or disclose that person's relationship to the Company, as required by section 3.1 of NI 43-101. The Company confirms that the preparation of the scientific and technical information that formed the basis for the scientific and technical disclosure contained in the Presentation derived from the Borralha PEA and the Vila Verde Technical Report were supervised by Vítor Arezes, MIMMM, QMR #703197, Vice President Exploration of Allied Critical Metals Inc., a Qualified Person as defined by NI 43-101. The Company will correct that omission in the Presentation and other applicable written technical disclosure. The qualified person references for this news release are set out below.

The Company acknowledges its responsibility for disclosure made by it or on its behalf and is committed to complying with NI 43-101 and applicable scientific and technical disclosure requirements. The Company has enhanced its internal disclosure review processes to support accurate, balanced, factual and non-misleading communications and to ensure that scientific and technical disclosure is based on information prepared by or under the supervision of, or approved by, an appropriately qualified person and includes the required disclosure of that person's identity and relationship to the Company.

The Company is undertaking an immediate review and correction of its website, corporate presentation, social media and other investor relations materials to address the issues identified above and remove other non-compliant or misleading technical information.

On May 19, 2026, the Company previously disclosed that, on May 15, 2026, the Company received a letter from Nasdaq notifying the Company that based on the closing bid price of the ordinary shares of the Company for the prior 30 consecutive business days, the Company was not in compliance with the continued listing requirement of Nasdaq under Nasdaq Listing Rules 5450(a)(1), which requires the Company to maintain a minimum bid price of $1.00 per share.

On November 20, 2026, the Nasdaq Listing Qualifications Staff notified the Company that the closing bid price of its ordinary shares had been $1.00 per share or greater for 10 consecutive business days, from November 9, 2026 to November 20, 2026. PACHA age-gated products will be America's first age-gated disposables

COSTA MESA, CA, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Charlie’s Holdings, Inc. (OTCQB: CHUC) (“Charlie’s” or the “Company”), an industry leader in the premium vapor products space, reported results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on recent business highlights.

Key Financial Highlights for First Nine Months 2026 (compared to first nine months 2025)

  • Revenue increased 19% to $11.3 million
  • Gross profit decreased 3% to $2.4 million
  • Operating loss increased 75% to $3.9 million

Key Balance Sheet Highlights as of September 30, 2026 (compared to December 2025)

  • Cash balance of $0.4 million, compared to $1.3 million
  • Total assets of $11.2 million, compared to $11.6 million
  • Total stockholders’ equity of $1.4 million, compared to $3.4 million

Management Commentary

“Because billions of dollars of illicit vapor products – made by Chinese manufacturers who thumb their noses at the FDA – have flooded the United States this year, Charlie’s sales and profits have taken a hit,” reported Henry Sicignano, President and CEO. “Fortunately, we have the inventory, and the opportunity, to reestablish growing, profitable sales in several states where regulatory enforcement has again become a priority. In this environment, we have redoubled our commitment to regulatory compliance as well as our initiatives to monetize the Company’s 678-SKU PMTA portfolio.”

Mr. Sicignano continued, “Big Tobacco ‘pod systems’ are outdated, provide very low puff counts, and offer few flavor choices. Charlie’s products are modern disposable products… offering much higher puff counts… and hundreds of flavors that adult consumers strongly prefer. For all these reasons, we believe Charlie’s PACHA product line is the best, most robust portfolio of PMTA products in the industry and will likely represent significant value to one or more Big Tobacco strategic partners in 2027.”

As previously reported, Charlie’s has made the well-considered decision to focus intensely on the two strategic priorities that matter most to Company shareholders:

1) Management has shifted its priorities from sales of the PACHAMAMA and SBX product lines to a laser focus on the beta test pilot of PACHA age-gated disposables. The Company has already received tens of thousands of finished age-gated PACHA products in its warehouse. Management has secured test-market purchase commitments from retailers. As soon as the Company’s software licensor completes final tests of its “second generation” consumer app, Charlie’s will begin shipping the age-gated PACHA product to stores. The Company expects that Charlie’s PACHA age-gated products will be America’s first age-gated disposables.

2) The Company has redeployed the priorities of one of Charlie’s largest shareholders. Ryan Stump, Charlie’s co-founder and former COO, has begun work to identify and pursue strategic transactions and/or partnerships with leading global tobacco companies to significantly enhance long-term value for Charlie’s shareholders.

Regulatory Developments

FDA Enforcement Priorities Guidance

In August 2026, the FDA notified Charlie’s that certain of its PACHA products (56 SKUs) for which PMTAs have been submitted have been tentatively identified for inclusion on the FDA's public-facing webpage of products for which the FDA generally does not intend to prioritize enforcement of premarket authorization requirements — a development the Company views as highly favorable. Inclusion on the FDA’s new list of “low-enforcement priority products” does not, however, constitute FDA marketing authorization, preclude case-by-case enforcement, or bear on whether any PMTA will ultimately be granted. Accordingly, Charlie’s intends to continue pursuing FDA review of its pending PMTAs and to comply with all applicable requirements.

FDA has validated age-gating as a pathway for the legal sale of flavored Electronic Nicotine Delivery System (“ENDS”) products

In May 2026, the FDA granted marketing orders for four Glas Inc. pod products, including “Gold” (mango) and “Sapphire” (blueberry) flavored, age-gated pods. This landmark development validates “age-gating” as a legitimate pathway for the legal sale of flavored ENDS products in the United States. However, Juul Labs filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Glas, Inc. and, under these circumstances, Glas’ newly authorized “fruit flavored” products are unlikely to go on the market in the near term; it is likely that Charlie’s PACHA age-gated products will be America’s first age-gated disposables.

Business Catalysts

Charlie’s plans to begin beta testing PACHA age-gated flavored disposables.

In December 2025, the Company signed a definitive licensing agreement to commercialize the first-ever AI-powered blockchain-based age-gating system for vapor products in the United States. Scheduled to beta test this year, the PACHA test-market initiative will incorporate the age-gating system in a special line of the Company’s flavored ENDS disposables; simultaneously, Charlie’s intends to amend certain of its existing PMTAs with the FDA for PACHA brand ENDS with the youth access prevention system.

Mr. Sicignano commented, “Charlie’s plans to launch PACHA products that have not yet received final FDA authorization follows the example set by one of America’s largest tobacco companies… In recent months, RJ Reynolds' Vuse business began selling four new fruit flavor pods (berry, fresh mint, peach, and watermelon), all of which were issued FDA Marketing Denial Orders (MDOs). Given that Reynolds has demonstrated it is willing to pursue flavored ENDS commercialization strategies, before final FDA authorization, we believe the strategic calculus for Charlie’s – and for our potential strategic partners – has improved. Dramatically.”

Charlie’s will monetize the Company’s PMTAs through new strategic partnerships

In 2025, in three separate transactions, Charlie's sold sixteen of the Company's PACHA synthetic nicotine PMTA products and related assets for $7.5 million in cash plus a contingent one-time payment of up to $4.2 million. In the last of the three transactions, the buyer purchased a single Charlie’s PMTA product for $1 million. Based on these sales, taking into account the fact that Charlie’s continues to own 678 PMTA products, and considering the interest other companies have expressed in Charlie's portfolio, the Company believes Charlie's remaining PMTA products, as a stand-alone asset, could have a monetary value that significantly exceeds the Company’s current market cap.

Financial Results for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026:

  • Revenue: For the three months ended September 30, 2026 revenue was $2.7 million, a decrease of $3.4 million, or 56%, compared with $6.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This decrease was primarily due to a significant decrease in sales of the SBX product line, from ongoing inconsistency in regulatory enforcement affecting customers’ desire for non-nicotine based vapor products. The decline in sales was offset by the launch of USA-made Pachamama line and sales of Pacha disposable products that are still under substantive review with FDA.

  • Gross Profit: For the three months ended September 30, 2026 gross profit was $0.1 million, a decrease of $1.5 million, or 92%, compared with $1.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

  • Total Operating Expenses: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, total operating expenses, including general and administrative, sales and marketing and research and development costs, were $1.8 million, a decrease of $0.2 million, or 10%, compared with $2.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

  • Operating Loss: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, operating loss was $1.7 million, compared with an operating loss of $0.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Financial Results for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026:

  • Revenue: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 revenue was $11.3 million, an increase of $1.8 million, or 19%, compared with $9.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was all due to the increase in nicotine-based product and nicotine alternative products sales. Sales of SBX, a non-nicotine, disposable vapor product which is not subject to FDA review, experienced a significant increase in the early part of 2026.

  • Gross Profit: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 gross profit was $2.4 million, a decrease of $0.1 million, or 3%, compared with $2.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

  • Total Operating Expenses: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total operating expenses, including general and administrative, sales and marketing and research and development costs, were $6.3 million, an increase of $1.6 million, or 34%, compared with $4.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

  • Operating Loss: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operating loss was $3.9 million, compared with an operating loss of $2.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Charlie's Chalk Dust has developed an extensive portfolio of brand styles, flavor profiles, and innovative product formats.

Third-quarter revenue of $11.2 million increased from $8.2 million in the second quarter; year-over-year results continued to reflect lower residential demand following the expiration of the Section 25D federal residential tax credit.

Commercial revenue increased 20% year-over-year to $2.7 million; SG&A expense declined 37% year-over-year to $4.3 million.

Results included $9.8 million of non-cash goodwill and intangible asset impairment charges.

SUNation continues to prioritize liquidity, cost management, and execution of its proposed merger with Suniva.

RONKONKOMA, N.Y., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SUNation Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: SUNE) (“SUNation” or the “Company”), a leading provider of residential and commercial solar energy systems, battery storage solutions and comprehensive energy services, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 (“Q3 2026”).

Third-quarter revenue increased sequentially to $11.2 million from $8.2 million, and gross margin improved to 30.8% from 26.1%, reflecting higher revenue across the Company’s New York and Hawaii operations. Year-over-year performance continued to reflect downward pressure from the residential solar market’s adjustment to the expiration of the Section 25D federal residential tax credit at the end of 2025 under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (“OBBBA”). Consolidated revenue declined 41% year over year, with lower residential revenue partially offset by growth in commercial revenue.

SUNation Reduces Costs and Advances Suniva Merger

The Company continued to manage its cost structure, reducing selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expense by 37% year over year. Results also included $9.8 million of non-cash goodwill and intangible asset impairment charges following an assessment of asset recoverability in light of lower forecast revenue and operating results. Including these charges, SUNation reported an operating loss of $11.7 million and a net loss of $11.8 million.

SUNation also continued to advance its proposed reverse merger with Suniva, Inc. (“Suniva”). SUNation currently anticipates closing in the first quarter of 2027, subject to satisfaction or waiver of applicable closing conditions and receipt of required approvals and regulatory clearances.

Q3 2026 HIGHLIGHTS

  • Revenue and gross margin improved sequentially
    Revenue increased to $11.2 million from $8.2 million in Q2 2026, and gross margin improved to 30.8% from 26.1%. Revenue declined 41% year over year, primarily reflecting lower residential installation activity.
  • Commercial revenue grew 20% year over year
    Commercial revenue reached $2.66 million, compared with $2.23 million in Q3 2025, primarily driven by growth in New York.
  • SG&A expense declined 37% year over year
    SG&A expense decreased to $4.33 million from $6.90 million, reflecting lower selling and marketing expenses and personnel cost reductions.
  • Net loss reflected non-cash impairment charges
    Net loss was $11.82 million, compared with $0.39 million in Q3 2025. Results included $9.82 million of non-cash goodwill and intangible asset impairment charges reflecting lower forecast revenue and operating results.
  • Suniva merger process advanced
    The companies amended their merger agreement during the quarter to address financing, stockholder approvals and closing requirements. Closing is currently anticipated in Q1 2027, subject to applicable conditions and approvals.

Commercial Growth Supports Revenue Diversification

The quarter’s sequential revenue and gross-margin improvement occurred within a residential market that continued to operate below prior-year activity levels. Residential revenue declined 52% year over year, while commercial revenue increased 20%. Commercial and service revenue together represented approximately 33% of consolidated revenue, compared with approximately 18% in Q3 2025.

The prior-year quarter also benefited from residential demand ahead of the year-end 2025 tax credit expiration, contributing to the year-over-year comparison. Management continues to emphasize commercial projects, battery storage, service and adjacent energy offerings as part of its efforts to diversify revenue.

Storage Opportunities Support Adaptation to Residential Market Changes

The expiration of the Section 25D federal residential tax credit at year-end 2025 under OBBBA continued to affect residential demand, installation volumes and financing economics during Q3 2026, following elevated activity ahead of the expiration. Lower installation volumes also increased fixed labor and overhead costs as a percentage of revenue.

Battery storage remains an area of focus. Hawaii’s Bring Your Own Device Plus program provides incentives for qualifying customers to add storage to existing or new rooftop solar systems. Hawaii Energy Connection’s battery attachment rates increased 13% year over year during the quarter.

Updated Asset Values and Liquidity Priorities

The Company’s impairment assessment reflected a material reduction in forecast revenue and operating results. Goodwill impairment charges related to the SUNation Residential and SUNation Commercial reporting units, while intangible asset impairment charges related to tradenames and trademarks across the New York and Hawaii businesses.

SUNation continues to prioritize cash preservation, disciplined working capital management and additional financing to support operations and maintain financial flexibility. The Company ended the quarter with $2.79 million in cash and cash equivalents and requires additional capital to meet its obligations and operating needs.

MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY

“Third-quarter revenue and gross margin improved from the second quarter as activity increased across our New York and Hawaii businesses,” said Scott Maskin, Chief Executive Officer of SUNation. “Commercial revenue grew 20% year over year, and commercial and service work represented a larger share of our business. Residential demand continues to reflect the change in customer economics following the expiration of the federal residential tax credit, and our teams remain focused on matching our offerings and operating structure to the market we are serving.”

Mr. Maskin continued, “Our priorities remain disciplined execution, customer service, cost management and liquidity. We are pursuing commercial projects, storage installations, service work, roofing and adjacent energy opportunities while managing expenses closely. We also continued to advance the Suniva merger process during the quarter, including an amendment to the merger agreement addressing financing and closing-related matters.”

James Brennan, SUNation’s Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operations Officer, said, “Higher sequential revenue supported gross-margin improvement to 30.8%, while year-over-year SG&A expense declined 37% following reductions in selling, marketing and personnel costs. Our reported results also included $9.8 million of non-cash impairment charges reflecting the effect of lower forecast revenue and operating results on the carrying value of goodwill and intangible assets.”

Mr. Brennan added, “Cash preservation, working capital management and access to additional capital remain essential. We ended September with $2.8 million of cash and cash equivalents, and our working capital position continues to require close management. We are evaluating financing sources and managing our obligations while supporting customer commitments and the proposed transaction.”

Mr. Maskin concluded, “We currently anticipate completing the Suniva merger in the first quarter of 2027, subject to the required conditions and approvals. Our immediate responsibility is to operate the business carefully through that process, serve our customers and preserve financial flexibility. The experience of our teams in New York and Hawaii, our customer relationships and our range of energy services remain important foundations as we navigate the current market.”

Q3 2026 FINANCIAL AND OPERATIONAL RESULTS

FINANCIAL RESULTS

  • Revenue
    Consolidated revenue was $11.20 million, compared with $18.99 million in Q3 2025, a decrease of 41%. Residential contract revenue declined 52%, partially offset by 20% growth in commercial revenue.
  • Gross profit and margin
    Gross profit was $3.45 million, compared with $7.21 million in Q3 2025. Gross margin was 30.8%, compared with 38.0% in the prior-year quarter, reflecting lower revenue and fixed labor and overhead costs that declined more slowly than sales volume. Gross profit and margin improved sequentially from approximately $2.1 million and 26.1%, respectively, in Q2 2026.
  • Operating expenses and cost reductions
    Total operating expenses were $15.16 million, compared with $7.46 million in Q3 2025, including $9.82 million of non-cash goodwill and intangible asset impairment charges and $0.46 million of Suniva merger transaction costs. SG&A expense declined 37% to $4.33 million from $6.90 million, reflecting lower selling and marketing expenses and personnel cost reductions.
  • Net loss
    Net loss was $11.82 million, or $1.81 per basic and diluted share, compared with $0.39 million, or $0.12 per basic and diluted share, in Q3 2025. The increase reflected the impairment charges and lower gross profit, partially offset by reduced SG&A expense. Operating loss was $11.71 million, compared with $0.25 million in Q3 2025. Impairment charges comprised $4.92 million of goodwill and $4.90 million of intangible assets. Amortization expense was unchanged year over year at $0.56 million.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue was $26.56 million, gross profit was $7.17 million and SG&A expense was $13.87 million, compared with $44.69 million, $16.48 million and $19.38 million, respectively, in the prior-year period. Net loss, including the third-quarter impairment charges, was $19.25 million, compared with $13.50 million in the prior year.

BALANCE SHEET AND LIQUIDITY

The following comparisons are with December 31, 2025, unless otherwise indicated.

  • Cash and working capital
    Cash and cash equivalents were $2.79 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $7.18 million at year-end. The Company had a working capital deficit of $5.35 million, compared with positive working capital of $1.07 million. Net cash used in operating activities during the first nine months of 2026 was $6.54 million, partially offset by $2.11 million of net cash provided by financing activities.
  • Payables and loans payable
    Accounts payable declined 23% to $5.66 million from $7.40 million. The aggregate carrying amount of current and long-term loans payable and related interest, including related-party balances, declined to $4.98 million from $6.60 million, reflecting repayments, the related-party debt conversion completed earlier in 2026 and borrowings under the affiliated revolving credit facility.
  • Credit facility extension
    On October 15, 2026, the maturity of the Company’s $1.5 million affiliated revolving credit facility was extended to April 15, 2027. Borrowings outstanding were $0.80 million at September 30, 2026, and the Company was in compliance with the facility’s covenants and other requirements at that date.

Total liabilities were $22.78 million, compared with $23.90 million at year-end. Current liabilities increased to $16.96 million from $15.41 million, while long-term liabilities declined to $5.82 million from $8.49 million. Stockholders’ equity was $8.69 million, compared with $24.35 million at year-end and $20.52 million at June 30, 2026, with the sequential decline primarily reflecting the third-quarter net loss, including impairment charges.

The Company requires additional capital resources and is considering all available options, including the ongoing strategic initiatives previously announced. The availability, timing, and terms of any additional funding remains undetermined.

OPERATIONAL RESULTS

  • Residential revenue
    Consolidated residential contract revenue was $7.53 million, compared with $15.66 million in Q3 2025, reflecting lower installation activity in New York and.
  • Commercial revenue
    Consolidated commercial contract revenue increased 20% to $2.66 million from $2.23 million, primarily driven by New York, where commercial revenue increased to $2.63 million from $2.23 million.
  • Service revenue
    Consolidated service revenue was $1.01 million, compared with $1.11 million in Q3 2025. Hawaii service revenue increased 54% to $0.37 million, supported by increased repair and replacement installations, partially offsetting lower New York service revenue.

By operating segment, SUNation NY reported revenue of $8.01 million and gross profit of $2.61 million, compared with $13.01 million and $5.29 million, respectively, in Q3 2025. HEC reported revenue of $3.19 million and gross profit of $0.84 million, compared with $5.98 million and $1.92 million, respectively. Hawaii’s lower residential installation volumes were partially offset by higher price per watt, increased battery attachment rates and service growth.

The Company continues to evaluate product offerings and financing options to support solar and storage adoption while pursuing commercial, service, roofing and adjacent energy opportunities.

STRATEGIC INITIATIVES AND PROPOSED SUNIVA MERGER

SUNation continued to advance its proposed reverse merger with Suniva during Q3 2026. The transaction, announced in June following the Board’s review of strategic alternatives, would result in Suniva becoming a wholly owned subsidiary of SUNation.

On September 4, 2026, the parties amended the merger agreement to address financing arrangements, stockholder approvals and closing requirements. The amendment revised SUNation’s closing net cash requirement to negative $2.5 million, subject to adjustment for potential capital raises, and added a proposed increase in authorized common shares from 1.0 billion to 1.5 billion to the matters requiring stockholder approval.

The amendment also provides for SUNation to use reasonable best efforts to repay or convert into equity up to approximately $2.61 million of specified related-party loans. Any conversion would be at $2.26 per share and subject to stockholder approval (with any related parties abstaining from the vote). These arrangements remain subject to the merger agreement, as amended.

The Company has confidentially submitted a registration statement on Form S-4 containing a proxy statement/prospectus relating to the proposed transaction. Closing remains subject to required stockholder approvals, effectiveness of the registration statement, Nasdaq listing approval and other applicable closing conditions and regulatory clearances. The timing and completion of the transaction remain uncertain.

Alongside the merger process, SUNation continued to manage its capital resources. During the first nine months of 2026, the Company completed a private placement generating approximately $2.7 million in gross proceeds for working capital and general corporate purposes, converted $1.2 million of related-party note principal into equity and made approximately $1.2 million of payments against third-party and related-party loans.

BUSINESS STRATEGY AND OUTLOOK

SUNation’s near-term priorities are to preserve liquidity, manage working capital, align costs with current revenue levels and advance the proposed Suniva merger. Management expects residential demand and installation activity to remain sensitive to customer financing economics and the market’s adjustment to the expiration of the Section 25D federal residential tax credit.

The Company remains focused on serving customers in New York and Hawaii while diversifying revenue through commercial projects, battery storage, maintenance and repair, roofing and adjacent energy services. Management will continue to evaluate financing alternatives to support operations and maintain financial flexibility as it pursues these priorities.

ABOUT SUNATION ENERGY, INC.

SUNation Energy Inc. (Nasdaq: SUNE) is a leading provider of sustainable solar energy and backup power solutions to residential, commercial, and municipal customers. The Company designs, installs, and services solar energy systems and related technologies, helping customers reduce energy costs, increase energy independence, and transition to cleaner energy solutions.

ROCKVILLE, Md., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Theriva™ Biologics, Inc. (NYSE American: TOVX), a diversified clinical-stage company developing therapeutics designed to treat cancer and related diseases in areas of high unmet need, announced today a reverse stock split of its authorized and issued and outstanding common stock, par value $0.001 per share, at a ratio of one (1) share of common stock for every thirty (30) shares of common stock, effective as of 11:59 p.m. (Eastern Time) on December 1, 2026 (the “Effective Date”).

The Company’s common stock will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis when the market opens on December 2, 2026. The reverse stock split was authorized by the Company’s Board of Directors on November 13, 2026. Pursuant to the laws of the State of Nevada, the Company’s state of incorporation, the Company’s Board of Directors has the authority to effect a reverse stock split without shareholder approval if the number of authorized shares of common stock and the number of outstanding shares of common stock are proportionally reduced. The Company will file a certificate of change to its articles of incorporation, as amended, with the Secretary of State of Nevada to effect the reverse stock split. The Company’s common stock will continue to trade on the NYSE American under the stock ticker “TOVX” but will trade under the new CUSIP number 87164U607.

As a result of the reverse split, each thirty (30) pre-split shares of common stock outstanding will automatically combine into one (1) new share of common stock without any action on the part of the holders, and the number of outstanding common shares will be reduced from 45,892,668 shares to approximately 1,529,756 shares without taking into account fractional shares. The number of authorized shares of common stock will be proportionally reduced from 350,000,000 shares to 11,666,666 shares.

The reverse stock split is being effected to ensure that the Company can meet the per share price requirements of the NYSE American, the Company's current listing exchange.

No fractional shares will be issued as a result of the reverse stock split. Stockholders who otherwise would be entitled to a fractional share because they hold a number of shares not evenly divisible by the one (1) for thirty (30) reverse split ratio will automatically be entitled to receive an additional fractional share of the Company’s common stock to round up to the next whole share.

Proportionate adjustments will also be made to the number of shares of common stock issuable upon exercise of, and the exercise price of, the Company’s outstanding warrants and stock options, and to the number of shares of common stock reserved for issuance under the Company’s equity incentive plans.

The Company’s transfer agent, Equiniti Trust Company, which is also acting as the exchange agent for the reverse split, will send instructions to stockholders of record who hold stock certificates regarding the exchange of their old certificates for new certificates, should they wish to do so. Stockholders who hold their shares in brokerage accounts or “street name” are not required to take action to effect the exchange of their shares.

About Theriva™ Biologics, Inc.

Theriva™ Biologics (NYSE American: TOVX) is a diversified clinical-stage company developing therapeutics designed to treat cancer and related diseases in areas of high unmet need. The Company’s subsidiary Theriva Biologics, S.L., has been developing a new oncolytic adenovirus platform designed for intravenous (IV), intravitreal and intratumoral delivery to trigger tumor cell death, improve access of co-administered cancer therapies to the tumor, and promote a robust and sustained anti-tumor response by the patient’s immune system. The Company’s lead clinical-stage candidate is VCN-01 (zabilugene almadenorepvec), an oncolytic adenovirus designed to replicate selectively within tumor cells, and to degrade the tumor stroma barrier that serves as a significant physical and immunosuppressive barrier to cancer treatment. For more information, please visit Theriva™ Biologics’ website at www.therivabio.com.

LINCOLN, Neb.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--As Lincoln gets ready for the Ohio State-Nebraska matchup, Bloom Energy is joining the community off the field to recognize the firefighters and first responders who help keep Nebraska’s capital safe.

On Friday, Bloom Energy visited Lincoln Fire & Rescue Station #1 and presented the department with a $10,000 donation. The contribution recognizes the more than 300 Lincoln Fire & Rescue personnel serving the city across 16 fire stations and supports the department’s continued work protecting the Lincoln community.

“Lincoln’s firefighters have been called on in extraordinary ways this year, from responding to historic flooding to helping fight the largest wildfire in Nebraska’s history,” said Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer at Bloom Energy. “We’re proud to recognize Lincoln Fire & Rescue and support the men and women who protect this community every day.”

“We’re very grateful to Bloom Energy for this opportunity. Employee well being is critical at Lincoln Fire and Rescue, but it’s not always something we have a lot of funding for when we also have equipment and other operational needs to prioritize,” said Dave Engler, Fire Chief, Lincoln Fire & Rescue. “This funding will allow us to invest directly in our members, whether that’s through physical and behavioral health programs, training and support following critical incidents, or resources to address challenges that come with shift work. We’re excited to put these dollars toward the health and well-being of our firefighters.”

Lincoln Fire & Rescue provides emergency services and community programs across the city. Its members also serve on specialized response teams, including Nebraska Task Force One.

This year, Lincoln firefighters have responded well beyond their day-to-day duties. In March, a Fire & Rescue crew deployed to Ogallala to help fight the largest wildfire in Nebraska’s history. In October, crews including the department’s Water Rescue Team rescued more than a dozen people during the flooding.

The donation reflects Bloom Energy’s commitment to supporting the communities it serves and recognizing the people and organizations that run essential services.

Bloom will also be on campus Saturday ahead of the Ohio State-Nebraska game as ESPN Radio’s College Football Campus Tour powered by Bloom Energy brings its live broadcast and interactive Fan Zone to Lincoln.
